Q: Translating Spanish stata dataset into English using Python A:

The problem is in how you rebuild the value label definitions after translation. You are probably using enumeration indices (0, 1, 2...) instead of the original numeric codes (4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10).

Fix it by preserving the original keys:

```python

# Wrong - loses original codes

for i, (code, label) in enumerate(value_labels.items()):

new_labels\[i\] = translated_label

# Correct - preserves original codes

for code, label in value_labels.items():

new_labels\[code\] = translated_label

```

Make sure when writing back to .dta you pass the original code-to-label mapping intact.

If you have 2,500+ variables, doing this manually is going to take a while even with the Google API. There is a tool called DataTranslator (datatranslator.net) that handles this automatically. It extracts all variable and value labels, translates them, and returns a corrected .dta file plus a .do file that reapplies everything. Numeric codes stay untouched.

Q: .gitignore exclude folder but include specific subfolder A:

Similar to this comment, none of the solutions and patterns worked for me; forcing Git (version control) to add the files and folders that should be excluded, worked:

git add -f .

Q: Calling a method from another instance of the same class A:

If you're just starting with C++, you owe it to yourself to look at std::vector as a replacement for the array. It'll make porting the testing code to the 12-conductor version that is probably just around the corner easier, possibly even a change to a config file rather than hacking the code. Plus std::vector is a lot more intuitive if you're coming into C++ from any language other than C. My fellow anonymous user started with std::vector for good reasons.

Q: Token is not provided A:

either in state (memory), session storage, or local storage... or as an httponly cookie so you can set it from the backend... but you haven't shown how you consume it... probably best to use specific methods built-in to your frameworks for doing this on frontend and back. (avoid "rolling your own" security) It'll also save you time having to write code for dealing with expirations, refreshes, "remember me", etc...
